page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-48 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor is equipped with 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a substantial 260 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 180.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 3.75 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in compute-heavy workloads. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2175.0 and a multi-core score of 18084.0, both placing in the strong tier. It demonstrates top-tier performance in image processing at 18872.0 and text processing at 2925.0. Cryptographic and compression capabilities are also notable, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 43744.82 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 34.08 GB/sec. For memory-bound operations, the server recorded a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 3389.0 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to 144.84 GB/sec.

Given the dedicated compute resources and advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, the c4-standard-48 is suited for CPU-based machine learning inference, software compilation, and database operations. It achieved 3296.88 tokens/sec for small LLM prompt processing and a strong Passmark database operations score of 21824.99. The absence of local storage and GPUs represents a tradeoff, making it less suitable for heavy storage-bound databases or GPU-dependent deep learning training. Qualitatively, its high compute density and advanced vector extensions provide strong resource efficiency for parallel processing, web serving, and enterprise applications without the overhead of specialized accelerator hardware.
